title: What does CredentialCreate do on XRPL?
abstract: Sourced explanation of CredentialCreate and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, CredentialCreate issues a provisional on-ledger credential to a subject account. [1]

CredentialType is issuer-defined binary data encoded as hexadecimal, not a globally unique legal classification. The subject normally must accept the credential before permission checks can rely on it. Expiration and URI can qualify the attestation. Trust depends on the issuer and purpose; a credential does not certify every article or grant universal payment-service approval. [1]

The CredentialCreate reference defines the operation-specific fields alongside the shared XRPL transaction fields. Account identifies the submitting account; signing authority, transaction cost and sequence handling still have to satisfy the ledger rules. A submitted transaction or an example in documentation does not establish a successful validated result. Where an amendment is required, confirm it is enabled on the intended network before relying on the feature. [1][2]

Author interpretation: before using CredentialCreate, compare the intended change with the current ledger state and keep the transaction hash with the resulting metadata. Treat unresolved outcomes as unresolved; submitting a replacement operation can create a second obligation. These are integration recommendations, not a report of a live test. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
